why: Every pane has a callsign its daemon drew (`otter`), unique on its machine, and may have a name somebody gave it, which need not be unique; both are taken wherever its id is, the callsign first, and a renamed pane keeps answering to its callsign. An id is unique across machines and never reused; a name is unique only among one daemon's live panes, so two machines can each have one, and `name@machine` then says which. The window and the CLI with no window both read typed text through this, so a pane is reached the same way whichever answers. Text that means no pane goes on as typed, which keeps every refusal for an unknown pane what it was and still reaches a pane made a moment ago by its id - unless a pane went by that name before a rename, when it is refused saying what that pane is called now.

cases.name: an id is the pane it names
cases.why: Ids stay the permanent address, and come first: a script holding one must reach that pane whatever anything is called.

cases.name: a name is the pane called it
cases.why: The point of a name: what you read off a row is what you type.

cases.name: a name somebody gave is matched whole, spaces and all
cases.why: A given name can be anything, and it is still an address.

cases.name: a renamed pane still answers to its callsign
cases.why: The callsign is what its row shows in blue and what agents were told to call it; renaming the pane must not strand either.

cases.name: a renamed pane answers to its given name too
cases.why: Whoever named it may type what they named it.

cases.name: a callsign is asked before a name somebody gave another pane
cases.why: A callsign is unique on its machine and a given name is not, so the one that can only mean one pane wins.

cases.name: a name is matched exactly, not by its case or a prefix of it
cases.why: A name that matched loosely would one day match the wrong pane. Completion is what saves typing, not guessing.

cases.name: two machines with the same name are told apart by the machine
cases.why: Each daemon draws its own words, so a laptop and a devenv can both have an otter; the machine is the name `muster window` prints beside the pane.

cases.name: a name two machines share is refused rather than guessed
cases.why: Picking one would send keystrokes to whichever came first; the refusal lists each so the next attempt can say which.

expect.refused: 2 panes are called "otter": otter@local (p1w3r07bsd), otter@devenv (p2w3r07bsd). Say which by its callsign, with the machine when two machines share it, or by its id; `muster window` lists them

cases.name: a callsign takes a machine like a name does
cases.why: Each daemon draws its own callsigns, so two machines can hold the same one whether or not either pane was renamed.

cases.name: a callsign two machines share is refused, naming each by callsign and machine
cases.why: The refusal offers what to type next, and for a renamed pane its callsign with the machine is the short address that works.

expect.refused: 2 panes are called "otter": otter@local (p1w3r07bsd), otter@devenv (p2w3r07bsd). Say which by its callsign, with the machine when two machines share it, or by its id; `muster window` lists them

cases.name: a name with an @ in it is matched whole before it is split
cases.why: Nothing stops somebody naming a pane `me@work`, and that pane must still answer to it.

cases.name: a name on a machine that has no pane by it is no pane
cases.why: The machine is part of the address: an otter elsewhere is not the otter asked for.

cases.name: text nothing answers to goes on as typed
cases.why: Whatever refuses an unknown pane goes on saying so in its own words, and a pane made a moment ago, which nothing has heard of yet, is still reached by its id.

cases.name: a name a pane had before a rename is refused, saying what it is called now
cases.why: An agent addressing itself by $MUSTER_PANE_NAME, which keeps the name it was started with, was told its pane had closed or came from an older window (kan a_2izzZ0Sag). It is pointed at the pane instead, and not taken there: the old name is free for another pane to take.

expect.renamed: nothing is called "kelp" now: the pane called that before is now called "🤖 A" (otter@local, p1w3r07bsd). Say what it is called now, its callsign or its id; $MUSTER_PANE holds a pane's id, which no rename changes

cases.name: a pane called a name now wins over one that was called it before
cases.why: A name freed by a rename can be taken by another pane, and whoever holds it now is who it means.

cases.name: every pane that went by a name before is named
cases.why: Two panes renamed away from one name are both candidates, and only the person typing knows which was meant.

expect.renamed: nothing is called "kelp" now: the panes called that before are now called "🤖 A" (otter@local, p1w3r07bsd) and "🤖 B" (maple@devenv, p2w3r07bsd). Say what it is called now, its callsign or its id; $MUSTER_PANE holds a pane's id, which no rename changes

cases.name: a former name with its machine points only at the pane on that machine
cases.why: The machine narrows a former name the way it narrows a present one.

expect.renamed: nothing is called "kelp@devenv" now: the pane called that before is now called "🤖 B" (maple@devenv, p2w3r07bsd). Say what it is called now, its callsign or its id; $MUSTER_PANE holds a pane's id, which no rename changes

cases.name: two panes on one machine sharing a given name are refused, naming each by its callsign
cases.why: A given name is a label and may repeat. The machine cannot tell the two apart, and their callsigns can.
